old: Its oldest form meant simply to strike something again and again.
One version of this word names a mixture made by repeatedly beating ingredients together.
It shares a root with 'bat' and even has a doublet called 'batture.'
clues: This verb for rough physical treatment was built with an old ending that signals an action done over and over, not just once.
Waves do this to a sea wall: strike it hard and repeatedly until it is damaged, far more relentless than a single knock or slap.
Its spelling also names the baseball player at the plate and the runny mixture poured for pancakes, each arriving by its own route from words for striking.
